::: {.why}
The components are not equally negotiable and the leverage comes from having a second process running, which is a scheduling decision made months earlier rather than a negotiating tactic.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the components of a quantitative research offer and which are negotiable.
- State what creates leverage and what you would do with an exploding offer.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Write out the structure: base, sign-on, guaranteed first-year bonus, discretionary bonus, deferred compensation and its vesting, and any non-compete. The sign-on and the guarantee move most easily, the base moves within a band, and the deferral schedule is usually firm. The non-compete is the term that most affects your next five years and the one candidates ignore.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Plan the timing: leverage comes from parallel processes finishing near each other, which means starting applications in a batch rather than sequentially. Write your target application window and the sequencing, and note what you would say to an exploding offer, which is a specific sentence rather than a strategy.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the two-sentence version of what you would accept and what you would decline, so the decision is made before the pressure rather than during it.
:::
:::
